newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RAPID REICHEL SCORES TWICE IN 56 SECONDS AS FLAMES BURN PENS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RAPID REICHEL SCORES TWICE IN 56 SECONDS AS FLAMES BURN PENS.

text.p: Robert Reichel scored twice in 56 seconds midway through the third period Thursday, including a penalty shot with 10 minutes left, as the Flames rallied for four consecutive goals in beating the Pittsburgh Penguins 7-5.

Reichel's power-play goal at 9:04 tied it and he was awarded a penalty shot at the 10-minute mark when he picked up the puck at the Pittsburgh blue line and broke for the net before being pulled down from behind by Francois Leroux.
Reichel skated straight at goaltender Tom Barrasso and deked him by faking a wrist shot before sliding the puck inside the right post for his third goal and a 6-5 edge.
German Titov scored his fifth goal after Pittsburgh pulled Barrasso for the final margin with 48 seconds remaining.
"He (Barrasso) made a good move, there wasn't much time and much room for me," Reichel said about the penalty shot. "He was moving at me and finally I put it in."
Calgary (6-4), which trailed 5-3 in the third period, has outscored rivals 18-9 in winning three straight.

Mario Lemieux had three assists for the Pittsburgh (2-7), which as lost four of their last five games. "There's not a whole lot of discipline out there and you play like that you're going to lose especially on the road," said Lemieux.

In Hartford, Jason Muzzatti continued his stellar play with 32 saves and Geoff Sanderson scored twice as the streaking Hartford Whalers defeated the struggling Mighty Ducks of Anaheim 4-1 for their fourth straight win.
Muzzatti, subbing for the injured Sean Burke, has been in the nets during the streak, stopping 85 of 89 shots.
At 5-1, Hartford is off to the best start in franchise history. The Ducks have opened the season 1-7-2 without star winger Paul Kariya, who is nursing an abdominal injury.
In Boston, Felix Potvin made 27 saves and Wendel Clark had a goal and an assist as the Toronto Maple Leafs continued their recent mastery of the Boston Bruins with a 2-1 victory.
Potvin lost his shutout on Jozef Stumpel's power-play goal with 5:12 remaining. "I just made the saves I had to make," Potvin said.
Tie Domi also scored for the Maple Leafs, who have posted consecutive wins following a five-game losing streak. Toronto is 5-0-2 in its last seven meetings with the Bruins.

In Buffalo, Donald Audette's power-play goal snapped a second-period tie and Derek Plante had two goals and an assist as the Buffalo Sabres squandered a two-goal lead but recovered for their third straight win, 6-3 over the Montreal Canadiens.

Montreal entered the game with the NHL's best power play (10-of-30) but was scoreless in five chances with the man advantage. "The power play didn't do well for us. We'll just have to go back at it," said Montreal coach Mario Trembley.

At New Jersey, Bill Guerin and Dave Andreychuk scored 16 seconds apart in the third period and Martin Brodeur made 28 saves as the New Jersey Devils beat the San Jose Sharks 3-1 for just their second win in six games.
Guerin, who has scored in three of the last four games, broke a 1-1 tie at 6:32 of the final period when his centering pass from behind the net deflected in off goalie Kelly Hrudey.
Andreychuk gave the Devils a two-goal cushion at 6:48.
"Yes, that was basically the game. That one minute, we made a couple of bad errors and New Jersey capitalised," said San Jose coach Al Sims.
At Tampa Bay, Ron Tugnutt made 32 saves for his first win in 20 months and Alexei Yashin had two goals and an assist as the Ottawa Senators cooled off the Tampa Bay Lightning 5-2.
Tugnutt, signed as a free agent in the off-season, posted his first victory since a 5-2 win over the Florida Panthers in February 1995 while with the Montreal Canadiens.
Steve Duchesne added a goal and an assist for Ottawa (3-2-3), who won for the first time in five road games.
"We want teams to respect the Ottawa Senators, we don't want teams to take us lightly," Duchesne said. "Tugnutt was unbelievable tonight."

In Chicago, Eric Weinrich's goal 3:55 into the third period snapped a tie and Tony Amonte and James Black each had a goal and an assist, leading the Chicago Blackhawks to their fourth straight victory, 6-4 over the St. Louis Blues.
The Blackhawks posted their first win in six games against the Blues at the United Centre (1-3-2).
Ed Belfour needed to make just 16 saves as Chicago dominated play, outshooting St. Louis 40-20.
Brett Hull's power-play goal 45 seconds into the third period tied the game 3-3, but Weinrich's second goal of the season three minutes later gave Chicago the lead for good.

In Los Angeles, rookie Rem Murray recorded his first career hat trick and Andrei Kovalenko scored a pair of power-play goals in a six-goal second period to power the Edmonton Oilers to an 8-2 rout of the Los Angeles Kings.
"They played a great two periods, they just woke up," Oilers coach Ron Low said.
Bob Essensa made 28 saves for his first victory since April 1994 with the Detroit Red Wings.
